samples.summary: New CLI is hard-incompatible with any already-deployed backend (unconditional `codeVerifier` + mandatory `state` echo)
samples.evidence: `login.ts:79` now always posts `{ code, codeVerifier }` to `/auth/cli/exchange`, and the backend's global pipe is `new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })` (packages/backend/src/main.ts:66-68). A backend deployed before this change has no `codeVerifier` on `CliExchangeDto`, so the exchange is rejected with 400 instead of returning tokens. The CLI also now refuses any callback that does not echo `state` (login.ts:243-246), which no pre-change backend sends — so the flow already dies at the callback and then again at the exchange. The CLI ships independently (`npx @wafflebase/cli`, `npm i -g`) and `--server` points at arbitrary self-hosted deployments (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md), so this breaks `wafflebase login` for every user whose server is older than this commit. The server side kept backwards compatibility (unchallenged codes still redeem); the client side has none — a `codeVerifier` sent only when the callback carried `state`, or a version probe, would restore it.

samples.summary: backend.md still documents `POST /auth/cli/exchange` body as `{ code }` only
samples.evidence: docs/design/backend.md:146 says "Body: `{ code }`" and lines 103-105 describe `GET /auth/github` with `Guard: AuthGuard('github')` and no CLI params, while the code now uses `GitHubAuthGuard` accepting `nonce`/`code_challenge` (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:59-85) and accepts `codeVerifier` (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.dto.ts). rest-api.md and cli.md were updated; backend.md and packages/backend/README.md:184-185,390 were not.

samples.summary: Agent-facing skill docs still show the old, unattributed error envelope
samples.evidence: packages/cli/skills/docs-read-content.md:86 shows `{ "error": { "code": "TYPE_MISMATCH", "message": ... } }` and packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:57 shows the same shape without `command`. Those exact paths now emit a single line including `command` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:202-208, packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:143-152), so the skill files an agent is fed describe the pre-change contract.

samples.summary: `ctx list` (and `status`) still report the not-logged-in failure as prose on stdout with exit 0, while its sibling `ctx switch` now envelopes it
samples.evidence: `ctx.ts:45-50` prints `console.log('Not logged in. Run \`wafflebase login\`.')` and returns 0; packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts:10-12 does the same. The change converted `ctx switch` to `errorEnvelope('UNAUTHORIZED', …)` on stderr with exit 1 (ctx.ts:62-71), so the same session condition is now reported two contradictory ways across the same command group — an agent branching on the documented one-line envelope (docs/design/cli.md:1079-1094, which claims every emitter goes through `errorEnvelope`) will silently mis-handle `ctx list`/`status`.

finding.summary: New CLI is hard-incompatible with any already-deployed backend (unconditional `codeVerifier` + mandatory `state` echo)
finding.evidence: `login.ts:79` now always posts `{ code, codeVerifier }` to `/auth/cli/exchange`, and the backend's global pipe is `new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })` (packages/backend/src/main.ts:66-68). The CLI ships independently (`npx @wafflebase/cli`, `npm i -g`) and `--server` points at arbitrary self-hosted deployments (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md), so this breaks `wafflebase login` for every user whose server is older than this commit. verdict.reason: The cited lines exist, but the finding is not a blast-radius blocker. (a) The claimed 400-on-exchange path is unreachable against an old backend: the state gate at login.ts:241-246 refuses the callback first, so the fetch at login.ts:76-80 is never issued — the reviewer's proposed fix (conditional codeVerifier) would change nothing. (b) The assertion that "the client side has none [no back-compat]" is factually wrong: login.ts:209-212 tracks the state-less callback specifically as "a backend predating the echo" and login.ts:293-308 fails closed with a message naming that cause and the --api-key fallback. (c) No in-repo consumer is broken: auth.dto.ts:13-16 makes codeVerifier optional, so current-CLI/current-backend and older-CLI/current-backend both work; the only affected "consumer" is a previously deployed artifact, and docs/design/cli.md:227-234 plus the task doc at 20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:47-53,87-90 document this one-way compatibility as the intended contract and explicitly reject the conditional-send/version-probe alternative as reopening the auth-code-injection hole. Real deployment-ordering consequence, but a deliberate, documented, fail-closed security contract rather than an unupdated caller or bypassed guard — out of this lens's lane.

finding.summary: New CLI cannot log in against a backend that predates this change: the extra `codeVerifier` body field is rejected by the global whitelisting ValidationPipe
finding.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:79` now unconditionally sends `JSON.stringify({ code, codeVerifier })` to `POST /auth/cli/exchange`. Any deployed backend built before this diff has `CliExchangeDto` with only `code`, and `packages/backend/src/main.ts:65-72` installs `new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true, ... })` globally — an unknown `codeVerifier` property makes that request a 400, not a successful exchange. Combined with the new loopback gate (an older backend also never echoes `state`, so `startCallbackServer` 400s its own callback and the login only ends at the 30s timeout), a freshly published CLI is fully broken against any self-hosted server that has not been upgraded. The docs (`docs/design/cli.md:218`) claim "Both are optional on the wire, so a new CLI still works against a server that predates them", which the `forbidNonWhitelisted` pipe contradicts. Fix belongs on the new CLI code: only send `codeVerifier` where the flow is known to be PKCE-capable, or fall back to a code-only retry on 400.

verdict.reason: The finding's central evidence is not present as described, and its mechanism is unreachable. (1) The quoted documentation claim is fabricated: docs/design/cli.md:218 reads "The two are not redundant: the nonce protects the *client*…", and the phrase "Both are optional on the wire, so a new CLI still works against a server that predates them" does not exist anywhere in docs/ (grep: no matches). The doc states the exact opposite under "Compatibility runs one way" (docs/design/cli.md:225-234): compatibility is deliberately one-directional, and "an older deployment upgrades the server or authenticates with `--api-key`". So there is no doc/code contradiction for forbidNonWhitelisted to expose. (2) The claimed ValidationPipe 400 on `codeVerifier` is unreachable against a pre-change backend: the CLI's own nonce/state gate at packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:240-246 refuses the state-less callback an older backend sends, so waitForCallback never resolves and the exchange at line 79 is never issued; the flow ends at the timeout handler (login.ts:293-308) which already emits a purpose-built message naming the stale-server cause. (3) No in-repo consumer holds the old contract: packages/backend/src/auth/auth.dto.ts:13-16 marks `codeVerifier?` @IsOptional, so the whitelisting pipe in packages/backend/src/main.ts:65-72 accepts it, and auth.controller.ts:168-169 forwards it to cli-auth.store.ts:114. The only true residue — a new CLI cannot browser-login against an un-upgraded self-hosted server — is an explicitly documented, intentional security trade-off (cli.md:229-234 says accepting the unbound code "would reintroduce the injection this section exists to close"), i.e. a design-fit/spec judgement expressly outside the blast-radius lane, with no broken caller in this repository.
